recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton

recQB9vpGAw3RmyQK.Bio: John Ech is a researcher and webmaster of Aether Force, a site exploring the borderlands of spirituality and science, including Electric Universe theory, suppressed technologies, and thinkers like Walter Russell and Rudolf Steiner. His work focuses on alternative, non-materialistic perspectives on light, energy, and the etheric forces connecting consciousness and the cosmos.
recQB9vpGAw3RmyQK.Name: John Ech

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Polarity and the Universal Breath", "body": "John opens with the principle he says runs through every talk he gives: polarity balanced by a neutral fulcrum, with physicality itself an expression of that tension. He traces it through Goethe's study of plant growth as expansion and contraction, then to Walter Russell, whose star draws in the cold of space through its poles and radiates it out at its equator, where the matter for planets is thrown off. Russell's laws, that cold compresses and heat expands, become a picture of breath. Chance links that balance to rhythmic breathing in meditation, and John calls the golden ratio, which Fibonacci numbers approach but never reach, God's lube."}, {"title": "Steiner's Sun and the Shapes of Sound", "body": "John presents Rudolf Steiner's view that a visitor to the sun would see nothing, only counter space that is less than nothing, pulling inward like Russell's star and acting as a prism that returns the planets' light to the cosmos. Steiner's planetary and zodiac seals, John notes, resemble cymatic patterns, the repeatable shapes vibration draws in sand or water, and his eurythmy dances letters to tune the body to the stars. Chance wonders whether Venus's five-pointed orbit shaped the seals, and John extends the idea to plants as antennas grounding celestial signals, arguing that the movement of stars and planets guides how physical form takes shape."}, {"title": "The Italian Inventor Few Have Heard Of", "body": "John introduces Pier Luigi Ighina, an Italian inventor whose work is mostly untranslated, and relays Ighina's view that light spirals between the sun and the Earth, and that a small plasma sun inside the Earth rings with the sun like a tuning fork in what Ighina called the magnetic rhythm. John recounts the claims made for him: shape power devices meant to calm earthquakes, a microscope showing brighter atoms pulling dimmer ones into their vibration, rain summoned over a rival's race days, and an apple tree turned into a peach tree. Chance, hearing of him for the first time, cannot decide whether he was a genius or a mad scientist."}, {"title": "Imagination, Attention and Ritual", "body": "Chance calls imagination a perceptual skill, a muscle worth training, and the conversation turns to Steiner's description of it as an organ of perception lying dormant in us. John describes Steiner's basic exercises, such as studying a rubber band for two minutes at the same time each day, and Chance frames the practice as sharpening attention to a spirit that is always present. John recalls Gurdjieff's challenge to notice yourself opening a door and calls ritual a geometric ordering of daily life, and both men push back on a spirituality that dismisses the material world as illusion, which John says Steiner would class as Luciferian."}, {"title": "Keely and Moral Technology", "body": "John closes the hour on John Keely and what he calls moral technology, devices said to run only when an operator with a coherent enough field is present. He describes one built by Dale Pond to a Keely design no one has managed to operate, though John says standing near it feels like a cool breeze. He recounts Keely's claim to have divided matter into at least 27 sub-levels governed by three streams from celestial bodies, and argues the popular Tesla quote about three, six and nine has never been found, pointing to Keely's harmonics instead. Chance, a little skeptical of Keely, wonders whether such technology could explain ancient architecture."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: John Ech of Aether Force returns to educate us on alternative perspectives about the Sun, the mysterious nature of light, and moral technology. We also discuss Rudolf Steiner and other thinkers, pondering the possibility that we may communicate with cosmic luminaries through the etheric filaments that connect us, and through the imagination portal within.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Galactic Nervous System", "body": "John lays out the electric universe paradigm as championed by the Thunderbolts Project and Donald Scott, where Birkeland currents, pairs of counter-rotating spiral filaments of electricity, stretch across the cosmos like neurons or mycelium. Galactic centers become Z-pinches that emit X-ray beams and toroidal flows rather than black holes swallowing everything, and the filaments branch like Lichtenberg figures along paths of least resistance. In his view the galactic center hands power to stars, stars relay it to their planets, and living bodies receive the smallest filaments, while Chance compares the pattern to a tree branching into smaller and smaller limbs."}, {"title": "A Sun of Condensed Matter", "body": "Drawing on Pierre Robitaille of Sky Scholar, John argues the sun is not a gaseous nuclear furnace but a body of condensed metallic hydrogen with a crystal-like lattice, which would explain why its surface is far cooler than the million-degree corona. He pictures Birkeland currents ringing that crystalline core like a bell, the way voltage makes a crystal vibrate through piezoelectricity, and Chance ties that vibration to heat itself. Chance compares this to the body regulating its own temperature, and John answers by pointing to George Merkle's largely scrubbed work on protein superlattices and biological fusion."}, {"title": "A Star Built in the Lab", "body": "The SAFIRE Project, the Stellar Atmospheric Function In Regulation Experiment, is what John calls the strongest evidence for an electric sun. Its team electrified a metal sphere held inside a magnetic field and, from a very low power input, reached stellar temperatures, formed symmetrical plasma discharges and double layers, and recorded new elements appearing on the anode. John treats it as an answer to critics who insist electricity could never power a whole star, while Chance suggests a sun may likewise need only a subtle input from the larger system it belongs to."}, {"title": "Geometry, Magnetism and Hard Light", "body": "John moves from Buddy James, whose golden ratio model of spheres collapsing on each other Donald Scott praised as the best geometry for a Birkeland current, to Michael Evans and his trion ray, and to Ken Wheeler's picture of magnetism as a torus paired with an hourglass dielectric field. Zooming inward raises capacitance until light congeals into what he calls hard light, and a black hole may simply be a massive body whose field is too strong to let it shine. He adds Wheeler's reminder that a wave is not a thing but what something does."}, {"title": "Bubbles, Sound and Cosmic Contact", "body": "In a bonus addendum John describes cavitation, where sound collapses a water bubble until it gives off light, and suggests stars might cavitate a cosmic water. He cites Mark LeClair's nanobubble jets producing transmutation and fusion temperatures, and redraws a waveform as a cross section of nested spheres. Earlier he recounts José Argüelles' thirteen galactic cones and radial plasmas that could let people link with Birkeland currents, while Chance prefers Steiner's inner doorway and argues that harmful modern technology is a plagiarized copy of abilities humans once held naturally."}]
